fit: reluctant to V：不情願做某事

hp.en: Kevin was reluctant to tell his parents about his low grade.
hp.zh: 凱文不情願告訴爸媽他考低分的事。

hp.en: The little girl looked reluctant to open the door of the dark room.
hp.zh: 小女孩看起來不情願打開那間陰暗房間的門。

extra.en: Mia was reluctant to speak in front of the whole class.
extra.zh: 米亞不情願在全班面前發言。

extra.en: He was reluctant to clean his room when his mom asked him.
extra.zh: 媽媽叫他整理房間時，他不太情願。

near.fit: bored (with 某事)：感到無聊，不接 to V。例：bored with the movie
tired of V-ing：厭倦做某事，不接 to V。例：tired of waiting
doubtful (about 某事)：懷疑、不確定。例：doubtful about the plan

hp.en: Amy is ambitious and wants the highest grade in every subject.
hp.zh: 艾咪很有野心，想在每一科都拿最高分。

hp.en: The ambitious manager hopes to run the whole company someday.
hp.zh: 這位有野心的經理希望有一天能經營整間公司。

extra.en: The ambitious young chef dreams of opening his own restaurant.
extra.zh: 這位有野心的年輕廚師夢想開一間自己的餐廳。

extra.en: Our team set an ambitious goal of collecting one thousand books.
extra.zh: 我們的團隊訂下收集一千本書的遠大目標。

hp.en: The museum guide warned us that the old vase was very fragile.
hp.zh: 導覽員提醒我們那個古老花瓶非常易碎。

hp.en: After her long illness, Grandma felt fragile and tired.
hp.zh: 久病之後，奶奶覺得自己脆弱又疲憊。

extra.en: Please be careful with this box; the glasses inside are fragile.
extra.zh: 請小心這個箱子，裡面的玻璃杯很易碎。

extra.en: Trust is fragile, and it takes time to rebuild.
extra.zh: 信任很脆弱，重建需要時間。

fit: loyal to 人或團體：忠於、對…忠心

hp.en: The assistant is loyal to her boss and never doubts him.
hp.zh: 這位助理對老闆很忠誠，從不懷疑他。

hp.en: Ben stayed loyal to his best friend even in the hardest moments.
hp.zh: 即使在最艱難的時刻，阿班仍然對好友忠心。

extra.en: Dogs are known to be loyal to their owners.
extra.zh: 狗以對主人忠誠聞名。

extra.en: She has stayed loyal to this little shop for ten years.
extra.zh: 十年來，她一直是這家小店的忠實顧客。

near.fit: honest (with 人)：誠實、不說謊，不接 to 人。例：be honest with me
sincere：真誠的，形容人、道歉、感謝。例：a sincere apology
frank (with 人)：坦白直率。例：be frank with your parents

hp.en: The salesman used a cunning trick to make us buy more.
hp.zh: 那位業務員用狡猾的手法讓我們買更多。

hp.en: The cunning thief fooled the guards and slipped out of the bank.
hp.zh: 狡猾的小偷騙過警衛，溜出銀行。

extra.en: The cunning fox tricked the crow into dropping its food.
extra.zh: 狡猾的狐狸騙烏鴉掉下牠的食物。

extra.en: He made a cunning plan to win the board game.
extra.zh: 他想出一個機靈的計畫來贏得這場桌遊。

hp.en: A mysterious voice came from the empty room upstairs.
hp.zh: 樓上空房間傳來一個神祕的聲音。

hp.en: Nobody knows who sent my sister the mysterious gift.
hp.zh: 沒有人知道是誰寄給我姊姊那份神祕的禮物。

extra.en: We found a mysterious letter with no name under our door.
extra.zh: 我們在門下發現一封沒有署名的神祕信件。

extra.en: The old house at the end of the street looks dark and mysterious.
extra.zh: 街尾那棟老房子看起來陰暗又神祕。

hp.en: Kevin was desperate to finish his report before the deadline.
hp.zh: 凱文拚命想在截止日前寫完報告。

hp.en: The swimmer made a desperate attempt to reach the shore.
hp.zh: 那名泳者拚了命想游到岸邊。

extra.en: After walking for hours, the hikers were desperate for water.
extra.zh: 走了好幾個小時後，登山客極度渴望喝水。

extra.en: Losing by twenty points, the team was in a desperate situation.
extra.zh: 落後二十分，這支隊伍陷入絕望的處境。

hp.en: My brother is so clumsy that he dropped his phone twice today.
hp.zh: 我弟弟笨手笨腳的，今天把手機摔了兩次。

hp.en: The waiter felt clumsy after he knocked over a glass again.
hp.zh: 服務生又打翻一個杯子後，覺得自己真是笨手笨腳。

extra.en: I was clumsy this morning and spilled milk all over the table.
extra.zh: 我今天早上笨手笨腳的，把牛奶灑得整桌都是。

extra.en: The puppy is still clumsy and often trips over its own feet.
extra.zh: 小狗還很笨拙，常常被自己的腳絆倒。

hp.en: My father was furious when he saw the scratch on his new car.
hp.zh: 爸爸看到新車上的刮痕時氣炸了。

hp.en: The customer was furious when the store refused to give her money back.
hp.zh: 商店拒絕退款時，那位顧客非常憤怒。

extra.en: My sister was furious when someone ate her birthday cake.
extra.zh: 有人吃了我姊姊的生日蛋糕，她氣壞了。

extra.en: The driver was furious about the long traffic jam.
extra.zh: 司機對漫長的塞車感到非常憤怒。

fit: grateful to 人 for 某事：對某人心存感激

hp.en: Amy was grateful to her coach for the advice.
hp.zh: 艾咪很感激教練的建議。

hp.en: The old man felt grateful to the nurse for taking care of him.
hp.zh: 老先生很感激護理師照顧他。

extra.en: I am grateful to my teacher for her patience.
extra.zh: 我很感激老師的耐心。

extra.en: The family was grateful to the neighbors for their help after the storm.
extra.zh: 暴風雨過後，這家人很感謝鄰居的幫忙。

near.fit: glad to V／glad that：高興，不接 to 人 for 某事。例：glad to see you
pleasant：令人愉快的，形容事物、天氣。例：a pleasant trip
satisfactory：令人滿意的，形容結果、表現。例：a satisfactory answer

fit: convince 人 to V／convince 人 that：說服、使相信

hp.en: Amy tried to convince her father to buy a smaller car.
hp.zh: 艾咪試著說服爸爸買一台小一點的車。

hp.en: It was hard to convince the police that the story was true.
hp.zh: 要讓警方相信這個故事是真的很困難。

extra.en: I could not convince my brother to share his snacks.
extra.zh: 我沒辦法說服弟弟分享他的零食。

extra.en: The doctor tried to convince him to sleep earlier.
extra.zh: 醫生試著說服他早點睡。

near.fit: suggest V-ing／suggest that：建議，不說 suggest 人 to V。例：suggest going home
explain 某事 (to 人)：解釋，人前面要加 to。例：explain the rule to me
describe 某事 (to 人)：描述樣子或經過。例：describe the man to the police

fit: abandon：拋棄、放棄（人、動物或計畫）

hp.en: The sailors had to abandon the sinking ship.
hp.zh: 水手們不得不棄守那艘正在下沉的船。

hp.en: It is cruel to abandon a kitten on the street.
hp.zh: 把小貓丟在街上很殘忍。

extra.en: Never abandon a pet just because it is getting old.
extra.zh: 千萬不要因為寵物變老就拋棄牠。

extra.en: Heavy rain forced us to abandon the picnic and go home.
extra.zh: 大雨迫使我們放棄野餐、回家去。

near.fit: relax：放鬆、休息。例：relax on the sofa
enlarge：放大（照片、尺寸）。例：enlarge a photo
broadcast：播放、廣播（節目）。例：broadcast the news

fit: accuse 人 of 某事：指控某人做了壞事。例：accuse him of lying

hp.en: The manager liked to accuse workers of breaking company rules.
hp.zh: 經理喜歡指責員工違反公司規定。

hp.en: It is not fair to accuse your neighbor of taking the money without any proof.
hp.zh: 沒有任何證據就指控鄰居拿了錢，並不公平。

extra.en: Please don't accuse me of lying; I'm telling the truth.
extra.zh: 請不要指責我說謊，我說的是實話。

extra.en: The store owner tried to accuse the boy of stealing candy.
extra.zh: 店老闆試圖指控那個男孩偷糖果。

near.fit: blame 人 for 某事：把錯怪到某人頭上。例：blame him for the mistake
charge 人 with 罪名：正式起訴（法律用語）。例：charge him with theft
criticize 人 for 某事：批評某人的做法。例：criticize her for being late

hp.en: The emperor wanted to conquer the whole continent.
hp.zh: 那位皇帝想要征服整片大陸。

hp.en: My cousin worked hard to conquer his fear of flying.
hp.zh: 我表哥努力克服對搭飛機的恐懼。

extra.en: She finally learned to conquer her fear of deep water.
extra.zh: 她終於學會克服對深水的恐懼。

extra.en: The army tried to conquer the small island.
extra.zh: 軍隊試圖征服那座小島。

fit: disguise oneself as ~：把自己打扮成別人或別的東西

hp.en: The two detectives wore uniforms to disguise themselves as cleaners.
hp.zh: 兩名警探穿上制服，把自己偽裝成清潔人員。

hp.en: The actor could disguise himself as an old woman.
hp.zh: 那名演員能把自己偽裝成老太太。

extra.en: He wore glasses and a fake beard to disguise himself as an old man.
extra.zh: 他戴上眼鏡和假鬍子，把自己偽裝成老人。

extra.en: The kids tried to disguise themselves as ghosts for Halloween.
extra.zh: 孩子們試著在萬聖節把自己打扮成鬼。

near.fit: hide 某物／hide from 某人：藏起來不被看到，不接 as。例：hide the key under the mat
pretend to + 原形動詞／pretend that：假裝某件事是真的。例：pretend to be asleep
conceal 某物或感情：比 hide 正式，不接 as。例：conceal the truth

fit: endure：忍受（長時間的痛苦或不舒服）

hp.en: Passengers had to endure a six-hour delay on the crowded train.
hp.zh: 乘客們得在擁擠的火車上忍受六小時的誤點。

hp.en: The hikers had to endure a freezing night without a tent.
hp.zh: 登山客得忍受沒有帳篷的寒冷夜晚。

extra.en: We had to endure three hours of waiting at the airport.
extra.zh: 我們在機場忍受了三個小時的等待。

extra.en: Some desert animals can endure many days without water.
extra.zh: 有些沙漠動物能忍受好幾天沒水喝。

near.fit: enjoy：享受、喜歡（愉快的事）。例：enjoy the music
receive：收到（信、禮物）。例：receive a letter
feel：感覺到（溫度、情緒）。例：feel cold

fit: forbid 人 to + 原形動詞：禁止某人做某事（也可用 from + V-ing）

hp.en: School rules forbid students to bring their phones to exams.
hp.zh: 校規禁止學生帶手機進考場。

hp.en: The landlord wanted to forbid the tenants to keep pets.
hp.zh: 房東想禁止房客養寵物。

extra.en: Many parks forbid people to feed the birds.
extra.zh: 許多公園禁止民眾餵鳥。

extra.en: My parents forbid me to use my phone at the dinner table.
extra.zh: 爸媽禁止我在餐桌上用手機。

near.fit: prohibit 人 from + V-ing：用法規正式禁止，不接 to + 原形動詞。例：prohibit drivers from using phones
ban 人 from + V-ing，或 ban 某物：公開下令禁止。例：ban smoking in restaurants
prevent 人 from + V-ing：讓某事無法發生（不一定是規定）。例：prevent the fire from spreading

hp.en: My brother loves to imitate our teacher's serious voice.
hp.zh: 我弟弟很愛模仿老師嚴肅的聲音。

hp.en: The comedian can imitate many famous people.
hp.zh: 那位喜劇演員能模仿很多名人。

extra.en: Young children often imitate their parents.
extra.zh: 小孩子常常模仿父母。

extra.en: This bird can imitate the sound of a ringing phone.
extra.zh: 這種鳥能模仿電話鈴聲。

hp.en: The lifeguard dived into the sea to rescue the child.
hp.zh: 救生員跳進海裡救那個孩子。

hp.en: A helicopter was sent to rescue the lost climbers.
hp.zh: 直升機被派去救援迷路的登山者。

extra.en: Firefighters arrived quickly to rescue the family.
extra.zh: 消防員迅速趕到，救出那一家人。

extra.en: The volunteers work hard to rescue stray cats.
extra.zh: 志工們努力救援流浪貓。

fit: tremble：發抖、顫動（不及物動詞，後面不接受詞）

hp.en: The boy's hands began to tremble when the teacher called his name.
hp.zh: 老師叫到他的名字時，男孩的手開始發抖。

hp.en: The whole building seemed to tremble during the earthquake.
hp.zh: 地震時，整棟大樓似乎都在搖晃。

extra.en: My legs started to tremble before I went on stage.
extra.zh: 上台前我的腿開始發抖。

extra.en: The windows began to tremble as the big truck passed by.
extra.zh: 大卡車經過時，窗戶開始震動。

near.fit: discover 某物：發現，後面一定要接受詞。例：discover a new island
invent 某物：發明，後面一定要接受詞。例：invent a machine
issue 某物：發布、發行，後面一定要接受詞。例：issue a warning

hp.en: Each hill was an obstacle on the way to the finish line.
hp.zh: 每一座山坡都是通往終點路上的障礙。

hp.en: Fear was the biggest obstacle for the young singer, not her voice.
hp.zh: 對這位年輕歌手來說，最大的障礙是恐懼，而不是歌聲。

extra.en: A fallen tree was an obstacle on the mountain path.
extra.zh: 一棵倒下的樹成了山徑上的障礙。

extra.en: Lack of sleep can be an obstacle to learning.
extra.zh: 睡眠不足可能成為學習的障礙。

fit: ancestor：祖先（很久以前的長輩）

hp.en: Her ancestor was buried in this village more than two centuries ago.
hp.zh: 她的祖先兩百多年前葬在這個村子。

hp.en: His ancestor sailed to Penghu on a small boat long ago.
hp.zh: 他的祖先很久以前搭小船到澎湖。

extra.en: My ancestor came to Taiwan from Fujian about two hundred years ago.
extra.zh: 我的祖先大約兩百年前從福建來到台灣。

extra.en: On Tomb Sweeping Day, my grandpa cleans the grave of his ancestor.
extra.zh: 清明節時，爺爺會去打掃他祖先的墳墓。

near.fit: pioneer：先驅、最早開拓某領域的人。例：a pioneer of space travel
generation：同一時期出生的一代人。例：the younger generation
founder：創立學校、公司的人。例：the founder of the company

hp.en: Her curiosity led her to explore the old library at school.
hp.zh: 好奇心驅使她去探索學校的舊圖書館。

hp.en: The scientist looked at the strange insect with great curiosity.
hp.zh: 科學家充滿好奇地看著那隻奇怪的昆蟲。

extra.en: The boy's curiosity about space made him read many books.
extra.zh: 那男孩對太空的好奇心讓他讀了很多書。

extra.en: Out of curiosity, I opened the old box in the attic.
extra.zh: 出於好奇，我打開了閣樓裡的舊箱子。

fit: nightmare：惡夢（睡覺時做的可怕的夢）

hp.en: The little boy woke up crying from a nightmare about a monster.
hp.zh: 小男孩從一場關於怪物的惡夢中哭著醒來。

hp.en: My sister had a nightmare about being chased by a huge dog.
hp.zh: 我姊姊做了一場被大狗追的惡夢。

extra.en: I had a nightmare that I was late for my final exam.
extra.zh: 我做了一場期末考遲到的惡夢。

extra.en: Last night I had a nightmare about falling from a tall building.
extra.zh: 昨晚我做了一場從高樓掉下來的惡夢。

near.fit: evil：邪惡、壞事。例：good and evil
crime：犯罪行為。例：commit a crime
hatred：強烈的恨意。例：hatred of war

hp.en: We read the legend of the Moon Festival in our history book.
hp.zh: 我們在歷史課本裡讀到中秋節的傳說。

hp.en: According to an old legend, a dragon sleeps under this mountain.
hp.zh: 根據古老的傳說，有一條龍沉睡在這座山下。

extra.en: There is a legend about a white snake living in the lake.
extra.zh: 有個傳說提到湖裡住著一條白蛇。

extra.en: The famous basketball player became a legend in his hometown.
extra.zh: 那位知名籃球員成了家鄉的傳奇人物。

hp.en: The twins were always looking for new mischief.
hp.zh: 這對雙胞胎總是在找新的惡作劇。

hp.en: The monkeys caused mischief at the temple almost every day.
hp.zh: 猴子幾乎每天都在廟裡搗蛋。

extra.en: The kids got into mischief while their parents were busy cooking.
extra.zh: 父母忙著煮飯時，孩子們開始調皮搗蛋。

extra.en: My cat is full of mischief and knocks things off the table.
extra.zh: 我的貓很調皮，會把東西從桌上撥下去。

hp.en: The soldier's sacrifice saved the lives of his friends.
hp.zh: 那名士兵的犧牲救了朋友們的命。

hp.en: My mother made a great sacrifice to send me to college.
hp.zh: 媽媽為了讓我上大學做出很大的犧牲。

extra.en: Parents often make a sacrifice for their children's future.
extra.zh: 父母常常為了孩子的未來做出犧牲。

extra.en: Giving up video games before the exam was a small sacrifice.
extra.zh: 考試前放棄打電動是個小小的犧牲。

fit: instinct：本能、直覺（不用思考就會做）；by instinct、act on instinct

hp.en: The mother bird protects her babies by instinct.
hp.zh: 母鳥憑本能保護雛鳥。

hp.en: The goalkeeper acted on instinct and stopped the ball.
hp.zh: 守門員憑直覺擋下了球。

extra.en: Birds fly south in winter by instinct.
extra.zh: 鳥類憑本能在冬天往南飛。

extra.en: My first instinct was to run, but I stayed calm.
extra.zh: 我的第一個直覺是逃跑，但我保持了冷靜。

near.fit: ability to V：做某事的能力。例：the ability to swim
energy：能量、體力。例：full of energy
a talent for 某事：天分。例：a talent for music

hp.en: After her parents died, her aunt became her legal guardian.
hp.zh: 父母過世後，阿姨成了她的法定監護人。

hp.en: The teacher acted like a guardian to the new students.
hp.zh: 老師就像新同學的守護者。

extra.en: A parent or guardian must sign this form.
extra.zh: 這份表格必須由家長或監護人簽名。

extra.en: The old tree stands like a guardian at the village entrance.
extra.zh: 那棵老樹像守護者一樣矗立在村口。

fit: take revenge on 人：向某人報復

hp.en: The prince wanted to take revenge on the man who killed his father.
hp.zh: 王子想向殺害父親的人報仇。

hp.en: He swore to take revenge on his rival after losing the match.
hp.zh: 輸掉比賽後，他發誓要向對手報復。

extra.en: Taking revenge on a bully will not solve the problem.
extra.zh: 向霸凌者報復並不能解決問題。

extra.en: The movie is about a man who takes revenge on the people who hurt his family.
extra.zh: 這部電影講的是一個男人向傷害他家人的人復仇。

near.fit: reward：報酬、獎賞（a reward for…）。例：a reward for finding the dog
report：報告、報導（a report on 主題）。例：a book report
return：回報、歸還（in return for…）。例：in return for your help

hp.en: The dictator was brutal to anyone who stood in his way.
hp.zh: 那名獨裁者對任何擋路的人都很殘忍。

hp.en: The winter wind on the mountain was brutal that morning.
hp.zh: 那天早上，山上的冬風冷得刺骨。

extra.en: The brutal heat made it hard to walk outside.
extra.zh: 酷熱讓人很難在外面走路。

extra.en: The movie shows the brutal side of war.
extra.zh: 這部電影呈現了戰爭殘酷的一面。

hp.en: The courageous nurse stayed with her patients during the typhoon.
hp.zh: 勇敢的護理師在颱風期間留下來陪病人。

hp.en: Everyone agreed that the young pilot was a courageous leader.
hp.zh: 大家都認為這位年輕機師是勇敢的領導者。

extra.en: The courageous firefighter ran back into the burning building.
extra.zh: 那位勇敢的消防員衝回燃燒的大樓。

extra.en: It was courageous of her to tell the truth.
extra.zh: 她說出實話，真的很勇敢。

hp.en: The zookeeper warned us that the tiger was fierce.
hp.zh: 動物園管理員提醒我們那隻老虎很兇猛。

hp.en: The final match between the two schools was fierce.
hp.zh: 兩校的決賽非常激烈。

extra.en: There was fierce competition for the last concert ticket.
extra.zh: 最後一張演唱會門票競爭非常激烈。

extra.en: A fierce dog barked at us from behind the fence.
extra.zh: 一隻兇猛的狗在圍籬後對我們吠叫。

hp.en: Her smile was genuine when she saw her old teacher again.
hp.zh: 再次見到老師時，她露出真誠的笑容。

hp.en: The expert checked whether the old painting was genuine or a fake.
hp.zh: 專家檢查那幅舊畫是真品還是贗品。

extra.en: This bag is made of genuine leather.
extra.zh: 這個包包是真皮做的。

extra.en: She showed genuine interest in my drawings.
extra.zh: 她對我的畫表現出真誠的興趣。

hp.en: Ben felt guilty after shouting at his mother.
hp.zh: 對媽媽大吼後，阿班覺得很內疚。

hp.en: The woman was not guilty, but she was sent to prison.
hp.zh: 那名女子是無罪的，卻被送進了監獄。

extra.en: I felt guilty for forgetting my friend's birthday.
extra.zh: 我忘了朋友的生日，覺得很內疚。

extra.en: The judge decided that the man was guilty.
extra.zh: 法官判定那名男子有罪。

hp.en: The lost child looked miserable as he cried in the rain.
hp.zh: 迷路的孩子在雨中哭著，看起來很可憐。

hp.en: He felt miserable living alone in the tiny basement.
hp.zh: 獨自住在狹小的地下室，他覺得很悲慘。

extra.en: I had a cold and felt miserable all weekend.
extra.zh: 我感冒了，整個週末都很難受。

extra.en: The rainy weather made our trip miserable.
extra.zh: 下雨天讓我們的旅行變得很糟糕。

hp.en: Even after winning, the champion stayed modest about her skills.
hp.zh: 即使贏了，這位冠軍對自己的實力仍然很謙虛。

hp.en: My grandparents live in a modest house in the countryside.
hp.zh: 我的祖父母住在鄉下一棟簡樸的房子裡。

extra.en: She is very modest about her success.
extra.zh: 她對自己的成功非常謙虛。

extra.en: They live in a modest apartment near the station.
extra.zh: 他們住在車站附近一間不大的公寓。

fit: timid：膽小的、羞怯的，可以放在名詞前（a timid boy）

hp.en: Kevin was a timid boy who was scared of talking to strangers.
hp.zh: 凱文是個很怕跟陌生人說話的膽小男孩。

hp.en: The timid kitten hid under the sofa because it was frightened by the doorbell.
hp.zh: 那隻膽小的小貓被門鈴聲嚇得躲到沙發底下。

extra.en: The timid rabbit ran away because it was frightened by our footsteps.
extra.zh: 那隻膽小的兔子被我們的腳步聲嚇得跑走了。

extra.en: A timid student like him is too shy to ask questions in class.
extra.zh: 像他那樣膽小的學生，太害羞而不敢在課堂上發問。

near.fit: afraid：害怕的，只能放在 be 動詞後（He is afraid.），不能放在名詞前
ashamed (of 某事)：感到羞恥，只能放在 be 動詞後，不能放在名詞前
scary：嚇人的，讓別人害怕（a scary movie），不是自己膽小

hp.en: My boss is stingy and gave us only cheap pens as gifts.
hp.zh: 我老闆很小氣，只送我們便宜的筆當禮物。

hp.en: The rich old man was stingy with his money.
hp.zh: 那位有錢的老先生對錢很小氣。

extra.en: My stingy neighbor never shares the fruit from his tree.
extra.zh: 我那小氣的鄰居從不分享他樹上的水果。

extra.en: Don't be so stingy; share some of your snacks.
extra.zh: 別那麼小氣，分一些零食吧。

hp.en: The concert hall looked magnificent with its golden lights.
hp.zh: 金色燈光下的音樂廳看起來壯麗極了。

hp.en: The eagle is a magnificent bird with huge wings.
hp.zh: 老鷹是一種有著巨大翅膀的雄偉鳥類。

extra.en: We watched a magnificent sunset over the sea.
extra.zh: 我們欣賞了一場海上的壯麗夕陽。

extra.en: The palace has a magnificent garden.
extra.zh: 這座宮殿有一座華麗的花園。

hp.en: She will always cherish the photo album her father gave her.
hp.zh: 她會永遠珍惜爸爸送她的相簿。

hp.en: My mother taught us to cherish our family.
hp.zh: 媽媽教我們要珍惜家人。

extra.en: We should cherish the time we spend with our grandparents.
extra.zh: 我們應該珍惜與祖父母相處的時光。

extra.en: I cherish the letters my best friend wrote to me.
extra.zh: 我很珍惜好朋友寫給我的信。

fit: confess (to 人) that：向某人坦白自己做錯的事

hp.en: The boy had to confess to his mother that he broke the vase.
hp.zh: 男孩不得不向媽媽坦白是他打破了花瓶。

hp.en: Amy decided to confess to her coach that she had lost the team's money.
hp.zh: 艾咪決定向教練坦白，她把球隊的錢弄丟了。

extra.en: He decided to confess to his teacher that he had broken the window.
extra.zh: 他決定向老師坦白是他打破了窗戶。

extra.en: I must confess to you that I didn't read the whole book.
extra.zh: 我必須向你坦白，我沒有讀完整本書。

near.fit: recognize 人或物：認出（看到就認得），不說 recognize to 人。例：recognize her voice
identify：辨認、確認身分。例：identify the thief
realize that：自己意識到，不接 to 人。例：realize that I was wrong

hp.en: The coach taught the girls how to defend themselves against attackers.
hp.zh: 教練教女孩們如何保護自己、對抗攻擊者。

hp.en: Kevin stood up to defend his friend when others laughed at him.
hp.zh: 別人嘲笑朋友時，凱文站出來替他說話。

extra.en: Soldiers defend their country in times of war.
extra.zh: 戰時，士兵保衛自己的國家。

extra.en: She always tries to defend her little brother.
extra.zh: 她總是試著保護弟弟。

fit: flee (from) 地方或危險：逃離

hp.en: The villagers had to flee from the erupting volcano.
hp.zh: 村民們不得不逃離正在噴發的火山。

hp.en: The prisoner managed to flee from the jail at midnight.
hp.zh: 囚犯在半夜成功逃出監獄。

extra.en: Many families had to flee from the flood in the middle of the night.
extra.zh: 許多家庭不得不在半夜逃離洪水。

extra.en: The thief tried to flee, but the police caught him.
extra.zh: 小偷想逃跑，但被警察抓住了。

near.fit: divorce 人：和某人離婚。例：They divorced last year.
separate A from B：把兩樣東西分開。例：separate eggs from milk
isolate 人或物：隔離，後面要接受詞。例：isolate sick animals

hp.en: The goalkeeper jumped forward to seize the ball.
hp.zh: 守門員向前一躍，抓住了球。

hp.en: The general tried to seize control of the government.
hp.zh: 那位將軍試圖奪取政府的控制權。

extra.en: You should seize every chance to practice English.
extra.zh: 你應該把握每個練習英文的機會。

extra.en: The police seize illegal goods at the border every year.
extra.zh: 警方每年都在邊境查扣非法物品。

fit: possess 某物：擁有（及物動詞，後面直接接東西或能力）

hp.en: Only a few athletes possess such amazing speed.
hp.zh: 只有少數運動員擁有這麼驚人的速度。

hp.en: My uncle always wanted to possess a rare old watch.
hp.zh: 我叔叔一直想擁有一支罕見的古董錶。

extra.en: Some people possess a natural talent for music.
extra.zh: 有些人天生擁有音樂天分。

extra.en: Few high school students possess their own car.
extra.zh: 很少高中生擁有自己的車。

near.fit: 某物 belong to 人：東西屬於某人，一定要接 to，主詞是東西。例：The car belongs to my dad.
occupy 空間或時間：佔用位置。例：occupy two seats on the bus
某容器 contain 某物：裡面裝著。例：This box contains old letters.

fit: pursue：追求（夢想、目標）；追趕（人或車）

hp.en: He left his hometown to pursue his dream of becoming an actor.
hp.zh: 他離開家鄉去追求成為演員的夢想。

hp.en: The officer began to pursue the thief across the park.
hp.zh: 警察開始穿過公園追趕小偷。

extra.en: She plans to pursue her dream of becoming a doctor.
extra.zh: 她打算追求成為醫生的夢想。

extra.en: The police car began to pursue the speeding truck.
extra.zh: 警車開始追趕那輛超速的卡車。

near.fit: request 某物：正式要求、申請。例：request more information
require：需要、要求（規定）。例：The job requires English.
beg (人) for 某物：乞求。例：beg for money

fit: scold 人 (for 某事)：責罵某人，後面直接接人

hp.en: The coach would often scold the players for being late.
hp.zh: 教練常常為了遲到責罵球員。

hp.en: The teacher did not scold Amy; she gave her another chance instead.
hp.zh: 老師沒有責罵艾咪，反而給她另一次機會。

extra.en: My mom will scold me if I come home late.
extra.zh: 如果我晚回家，媽媽會罵我。

extra.en: Teachers should not scold students in front of the class.
extra.zh: 老師不應該在全班面前責罵學生。

near.fit: complain about 某事／to 人：抱怨，不能直接接人。例：complain about the noise
argue with 人／argue that：爭論，不能直接接人。例：argue with my sister
quarrel with 人：吵架，不能直接接人。例：quarrel with a friend

fit: overcome：克服（困難、恐懼、缺點）

hp.en: Ben had to overcome his fear of heights.
hp.zh: 阿班必須克服懼高症。

hp.en: With practice, my sister was finally able to overcome her fear of dogs.
hp.zh: 經過練習，我姊姊終於克服了對狗的恐懼。

extra.en: She worked hard to overcome her fear of public speaking.
extra.zh: 她努力克服對公開演講的恐懼。

extra.en: Our team can overcome any problem if we work together.
extra.zh: 只要齊心合作，我們的團隊能克服任何問題。

near.fit: persuade 人 to V：說服某人，受詞是人。例：persuade him to stay
obey：服從（命令、規則、父母）。例：obey the rules
admire：佩服、欣賞（人或作品）。例：admire her courage

hp.en: The brave firefighters deserve our thanks.
hp.zh: 勇敢的消防員值得我們感謝。

hp.en: Hard-working employees deserve better pay.
hp.zh: 認真工作的員工應該得到更好的薪水。

extra.en: You worked so hard; you deserve a good rest.
extra.zh: 你那麼努力，值得好好休息一下。

extra.en: All children deserve a safe place to live.
extra.zh: 所有孩子都應該擁有安全的住處。

hp.en: They called him a coward, but he proved them wrong.
hp.zh: 他們罵他是膽小鬼，但他證明他們錯了。

hp.en: The captain was a coward who left the ship before the passengers.
hp.zh: 那名船長是個懦夫，比乘客先棄船逃走。

extra.en: He is not a coward; he just needs more time.
extra.zh: 他不是膽小鬼，只是需要多一點時間。

extra.en: Only a coward would run away and leave his friends behind.
extra.zh: 只有懦夫才會丟下朋友自己逃跑。

hp.en: She was angry about the cruelty toward farm animals.
hp.zh: 她對虐待農場動物的殘忍行為感到憤怒。

hp.en: The king's cruelty shocked even his own soldiers.
hp.zh: 國王的殘忍連他的士兵都感到震驚。

extra.en: The law protects animals from cruelty.
extra.zh: 法律保護動物免受虐待。

extra.en: Everyone was shocked by his cruelty to the stray dog.
extra.zh: 大家都對他虐待流浪狗的殘忍行為感到震驚。

hp.en: Even as a prisoner, the old leader kept his dignity.
hp.zh: 即使身為囚犯，那位老領袖仍保有尊嚴。

hp.en: She believes that all workers should have dignity and fair pay.
hp.zh: 她認為所有勞工都應該擁有尊嚴和合理的薪水。

extra.en: Every person should be treated with dignity.
extra.zh: 每個人都應該受到有尊嚴的對待。

extra.en: She lost the game but left the court with dignity.
extra.zh: 她輸了比賽，但仍有尊嚴地離開球場。

fit: grief：失去親友或心愛事物的悲傷

hp.en: The whole family was filled with grief after Grandma died.
hp.zh: 奶奶過世後，全家人充滿悲傷。

hp.en: He could not hide his grief when his old dog died.
hp.zh: 他的老狗死時，他藏不住心中的悲痛。

extra.en: Time can slowly ease her grief over losing a pet.
extra.zh: 時間能慢慢減輕她失去寵物的悲傷。

extra.en: She wrote a song to express her grief.
extra.zh: 她寫了一首歌來表達自己的悲傷。

near.fit: injury：身體受傷。例：a knee injury
wound：傷口（刀傷、槍傷）。例：clean the wound
damage：東西被破壞的損害（不可數）。例：storm damage

hp.en: Amy's jealousy grew when her friend won the prize.
hp.zh: 朋友得獎後，艾咪的嫉妒心愈來愈強。

hp.en: He could not hide his jealousy of his brother's success.
hp.zh: 他藏不住對哥哥成功的嫉妒。

extra.en: Her jealousy began when her sister got a new phone.
extra.zh: 姊姊拿到新手機後，她就開始嫉妒了。

extra.en: Try not to let jealousy ruin your friendships.
extra.zh: 試著別讓嫉妒毀了你的友誼。

hp.en: The judge showed mercy and gave the young man a second chance.
hp.zh: 法官心存憐憫，給了那個年輕人第二次機會。

hp.en: The invaders showed no mercy to their enemies.
hp.zh: 侵略者對敵人毫不留情。

extra.en: The king showed mercy and set the prisoner free.
extra.zh: 國王大發慈悲，釋放了那名囚犯。

extra.en: The storm showed no mercy to the small fishing boats.
extra.zh: 暴風雨對小漁船毫不留情。

hp.en: Using the teachers' lounge was a privilege for the class leaders.
hp.zh: 使用教師休息室是班級幹部的特權。

hp.en: It was a privilege for me to learn from such a great pianist.
hp.zh: 能向這麼優秀的鋼琴家學習，對我來說是一種榮幸。

extra.en: Driving a car is a privilege, not a right.
extra.zh: 開車是一種特權，而不是權利。

extra.en: It is a privilege to speak at the graduation ceremony.
extra.zh: 能在畢業典禮上致詞是一種榮幸。

fit: a good/bad reputation (for/as ~)：名聲、口碑，可數，可以加 a

hp.en: Mr. Chen has a reputation as a kind and patient doctor.
hp.zh: 陳先生有著親切又有耐心的好醫生名聲。

hp.en: Our math teacher has a reputation for being very strict.
hp.zh: 我們的數學老師是出了名的嚴格。

extra.en: The restaurant has a good reputation for its noodles.
extra.zh: 這家餐廳的麵食口碑很好。

extra.en: Telling lies can give you a bad reputation.
extra.zh: 說謊會讓你的名聲變差。

near.fit: fame 不可數，不說 a fame。指出名這件事。例：win fame as a singer
an honor to + 原形動詞：做某事是一種榮幸；或 in honor of ~。例：It's an honor to meet you.
glory 不可數，指偉大成就帶來的榮耀。例：the glory of winning the gold medal

fit: in triumph：得勝地、得意洋洋地

hp.en: The fans cheered in triumph when their team won the cup.
hp.zh: 球隊奪冠時，球迷歡呼慶祝勝利。

hp.en: The winner ran around the field in triumph, holding a flag.
hp.zh: 優勝者舉著旗子，得意洋洋地繞著操場跑。

extra.en: Dad raised his arms in triumph as he finished the marathon.
extra.zh: 爸爸跑完馬拉松時，得意地舉起雙臂。

extra.en: The team returned home in triumph after the final.
extra.zh: 決賽後，球隊凱旋歸來。

near.fit: profit：做生意賺的錢。例：make a profit
interest：興趣（in…）；銀行的利息。例：an interest in music
benefit：好處（for the benefit of…）。例：the benefits of exercise

fit: companion：陪伴你的同伴（人或動物）

hp.en: This old cat was my grandmother's loyal companion for many years.
hp.zh: 這隻老貓多年來都是奶奶忠實的夥伴。

hp.en: The small dog was the farmer's faithful companion in the fields.
hp.zh: 那隻小狗是農夫在田裡忠實的同伴。

extra.en: My dog is my best companion on long walks.
extra.zh: 散步走很遠時，我的狗是我最好的同伴。

extra.en: On the long train ride to Hualien, her cat was her only companion.
extra.zh: 搭火車去花蓮的漫長路上，她的貓是她唯一的旅伴。

near.fit: colleague：同事，一起工作的人。例：my colleague at the office
competitor：參加比賽或商業競爭的人。例：a strong competitor
opponent：比賽、辯論中跟你對抗的人。例：beat his opponent

hp.en: The manager gave Kevin a harsh look after he spilled the coffee.
hp.zh: 凱文打翻咖啡後，經理嚴厲地瞪了他一眼。

hp.en: These farmers live in a harsh place high in the cold mountains.
hp.zh: 這些農夫住在寒冷高山上一個環境惡劣的地方。

extra.en: The coach's words were harsh, but they helped us improve.
extra.zh: 教練的話很嚴厲，但幫助我們進步。

extra.en: Few plants can grow in such a harsh climate.
extra.zh: 很少植物能在這麼惡劣的氣候中生長。

hp.en: The secretary arrived with an urgent letter for the president.
hp.zh: 祕書帶來一封要給總裁的緊急信件。

hp.en: The principal called an urgent meeting of all the teachers.
hp.zh: 校長召開全體老師的緊急會議。

extra.en: Please call me back; it's urgent.
extra.zh: 請回電給我，事情很緊急。

extra.en: The patient needs urgent care at the hospital.
extra.zh: 這位病人需要在醫院接受緊急治療。

hp.en: The librarian did a thorough search for the missing book.
hp.zh: 圖書館員徹底搜尋那本遺失的書。

hp.en: The guard made a thorough check of every visitor's bag.
hp.zh: 警衛仔細檢查了每位訪客的包包。

extra.en: The doctor gave me a thorough checkup.
extra.zh: 醫生幫我做了一次徹底的健康檢查。

extra.en: We gave the house a thorough cleaning before New Year.
extra.zh: 過年前我們把房子徹底打掃了一遍。

fit: tolerate 人或事：容忍、忍受（及物，後面直接接受詞）

hp.en: The principal would not tolerate cheating in her school.
hp.zh: 校長不容許學校裡有人作弊。

hp.en: My sister could not tolerate her roommate's bad habits.
hp.zh: 我姊姊無法容忍室友的壞習慣。

extra.en: Our teacher does not tolerate rude behavior.
extra.zh: 我們老師不容忍無禮的行為。

extra.en: Some plants can tolerate very little sunlight.
extra.zh: 有些植物能忍受很少的日照。

near.fit: cope with 某事：應付、處理，一定要加 with。例：cope with stress
sympathize with 人：同情、體諒，一定要加 with。例：sympathize with her
complain about 某事：抱怨，要加 about。例：complain about the food

fit: devote 時間／生命 to + 名詞或 V-ing：把…奉獻給、投入於

hp.en: The nurse decided to devote her free time to helping the elderly.
hp.zh: 那位護理師決定把空閒時間都用來幫助長者。

hp.en: The coach wanted the team to devote every weekend to basketball practice.
hp.zh: 教練希望球隊把每個週末都投入籃球練習。

extra.en: My grandmother chose to devote her life to teaching.
extra.zh: 我奶奶選擇把一生奉獻給教育。

extra.en: I plan to devote two hours a day to studying English.
extra.zh: 我打算每天花兩小時學英文。

near.fit: spend 時間 V-ing／spend 時間 on 某事：花時間，不用 to。例：spend an hour reading
invest 錢或時間 in 某事：投資，用 in 不用 to。例：invest time in learning
waste 時間 V-ing／waste 時間 on 某事：浪費，不用 to。例：waste time on games

fit: interfere with／in 某事：干涉、妨礙（不及物，要加 with 或 in）

hp.en: The teacher told us not to interfere with the experiment.
hp.zh: 老師告訴我們不要干擾實驗。

hp.en: The mayor did not want the company to interfere with the election.
hp.zh: 市長不希望那家公司干預選舉。

extra.en: Don't let video games interfere with your schoolwork.
extra.zh: 別讓電動妨礙你的課業。

extra.en: My parents try not to interfere in my choice of friends.
extra.zh: 爸媽盡量不干涉我交什麼朋友。

near.fit: disturb 人：打擾，後面直接接受詞，不加 with／in。例：Don't disturb me.
interrupt 人或事：打斷說話或進行中的事，直接接受詞。例：interrupt the teacher
prevent 人 from V-ing：阻止某人做某事。例：prevent him from leaving

hp.en: The two families have lived in harmony for many years.
hp.zh: 這兩家人多年來和諧相處。

hp.en: The soft music filled the room with peace and harmony.
hp.zh: 輕柔的音樂讓房間充滿平靜與和諧。

extra.en: The choir sang in perfect harmony.
extra.zh: 合唱團唱出完美的和聲。

extra.en: People of different cultures can live in harmony.
extra.zh: 不同文化的人可以和諧共處。

fit: privacy：隱私，不可數，不加 a、不加 s（need privacy、for privacy）

hp.en: The nurse closed the curtains around the bed for privacy.
hp.zh: 護理師拉上病床的簾子，保護隱私。

hp.en: Students in the crowded dormitory do not have much privacy.
hp.zh: 擁擠宿舍裡的學生沒有太多隱私。

extra.en: Teenagers often want more privacy from their parents.
extra.zh: 青少年常希望父母給他們更多隱私。

extra.en: Please knock first because I need privacy in my room.
extra.zh: 請先敲門，因為我在房間裡需要隱私。

near.fit: a secret／secrets：祕密，可數，單數前面要有 a 或 my 等字。例：keep a secret
an affair／affairs：事務，可數，常用複數。例：family affairs
an individual：個人（指人，可數）。例：each individual

hp.en: There was a lot of tension in the gym before the winner was announced.
hp.zh: 優勝者揭曉前，體育館裡氣氛非常緊張。

hp.en: The tension between the two neighbors grew every year.
hp.zh: 這兩位鄰居之間的緊張關係一年比一年嚴重。

extra.en: You could feel the tension in the classroom before the exam.
extra.zh: 考試前，教室裡的緊張氣氛感覺得到。

extra.en: A short walk can help reduce tension after a long day.
extra.zh: 散步一下能幫助舒緩一整天的緊繃。

fit: catch／get／have a glimpse of 某物：瞥見（用 of）

hp.en: I caught a glimpse of a deer near the road.
hp.zh: 我瞥見路邊有一隻鹿。

hp.en: In the crowd, I had a glimpse of my old friend waving at me.
hp.zh: 在人群中，我瞥見老朋友對我揮手。

extra.en: We caught a glimpse of the famous singer as her car drove by.
extra.zh: 那位知名歌手的車經過時，我們瞥見了她。

extra.en: From the plane, I got a glimpse of Taipei 101.
extra.zh: 從飛機上，我瞥見了台北 101。

near.fit: have／take a look at 某物：看一看，用 at 不用 of。例：take a look at this
take／cast a glance at 某物：瞄一眼，用 at；也不說 catch a glance。例：a glance at the clock
give 人 a stare：盯著看，不說 catch a stare of。例：give him a cold stare

hp.en: My brother thought the fortune teller's predictions were absurd.
hp.zh: 我哥哥認為算命師的預言很荒謬。

hp.en: The idea that the moon is made of cheese is absurd.
hp.zh: 說月亮是乳酪做的，這種想法很荒謬。

extra.en: It is absurd to wear a coat on such a hot day.
extra.zh: 這麼熱的天穿大衣真是荒謬。

extra.en: His excuse for being late was completely absurd.
extra.zh: 他遲到的藉口完全荒謬。

hp.en: The rich boy was arrogant and often laughed at other students.
hp.zh: 那個有錢的男孩很傲慢，常嘲笑其他同學。

hp.en: The director was too arrogant to admit his mistakes.
hp.zh: 那位主管太傲慢了，不肯承認自己的錯。

extra.en: The arrogant player refused to shake hands after the game.
extra.zh: 那位傲慢的球員賽後拒絕握手。

extra.en: Being smart does not give you the right to be arrogant.
extra.zh: 聰明不代表你有權傲慢。

fit: be vulnerable to + 名詞：容易受到…的傷害

hp.en: Without a firewall, computers are vulnerable to viruses.
hp.zh: 沒有防火牆，電腦很容易受到病毒攻擊。

hp.en: Young trees are vulnerable to strong winds.
hp.zh: 小樹很容易被強風吹壞。

extra.en: Old people are more vulnerable to the flu.
extra.zh: 老年人比較容易得流感。

extra.en: Small animals are vulnerable to hawks when they leave their nests.
extra.zh: 小動物離開巢穴時，很容易被老鷹攻擊。

near.fit: be likely to + 原形動詞：可能會…，to 後面接動詞不接名詞。例：It is likely to rain.
be apt to + 原形動詞：容易…（傾向），to 後面接動詞。例：apt to forget
It is easy to + 原形動詞：做某事很容易（主詞通常是 it 或事情），不接 to + 名詞。例：It is easy to learn.

fit: betray 人或祕密：背叛、出賣（及物，後面直接接受詞）

hp.en: The general chose to betray his king.
hp.zh: 那位將軍選擇背叛他的國王。

hp.en: Amy would never betray the people who trusted her.
hp.zh: 艾咪絕不會背叛信任她的人。

extra.en: A true friend will never betray your secret.
extra.zh: 真正的朋友絕不會出賣你的祕密。

extra.en: The spy decided to betray his country for money.
extra.zh: 這名間諜為了錢決定背叛他的國家。

near.fit: rebel against 人或權威：反叛，一定要加 against。例：rebel against the king
disagree with 人或意見：不同意，一定要加 with。例：disagree with my brother
object to 某事：反對，一定要加 to。例：object to the plan

fit: adore 人或物：非常喜愛（及物，後面直接接受詞）

hp.en: My little sister seems to adore every animal she meets.
hp.zh: 我妹妹似乎很喜愛她遇到的每一種動物。

hp.en: The younger students adore Ms. Wang's art lessons.
hp.zh: 低年級學生非常喜歡王老師的美術課。

extra.en: Children adore this cartoon character.
extra.zh: 小朋友非常喜愛這個卡通角色。

extra.en: I adore the smell of fresh bread in the morning.
extra.zh: 我非常喜歡早上新鮮麵包的香味。

near.fit: care about 人或事：在乎，要加 about。例：care about your health
long for 某物／long to V：渴望，要加 for 或 to。例：long for home
yearn for 某物／yearn to V：嚮往，要加 for 或 to。例：yearn for freedom

hp.en: The runner leaned forward and began to accelerate.
hp.zh: 跑者身體往前傾，開始加速。

hp.en: The train began to accelerate as it left the station.
hp.zh: 火車駛離車站時開始加速。

extra.en: The car began to accelerate on the highway.
extra.zh: 車子在高速公路上開始加速。

extra.en: Warm weather can accelerate the growth of plants.
extra.zh: 溫暖的天氣能加速植物生長。

hp.en: The grandmother showed great affection for all her grandchildren.
hp.zh: 奶奶非常疼愛所有的孫子孫女。

hp.en: The farmer had deep affection for his old horse.
hp.zh: 農夫非常疼愛他的老馬。

extra.en: My cat shows affection by rubbing against my legs.
extra.zh: 我的貓會磨蹭我的腿來表達喜愛。

extra.en: Grandpa never says much, but we can feel his affection.
extra.zh: 爺爺話不多，但我們感受得到他的關愛。

fit: have an allergy to 某物：對…過敏（用 to）

hp.en: Kevin joked that he had an allergy to homework.
hp.zh: 凱文開玩笑說他對功課過敏。

hp.en: The doctor warned that some children might have an allergy to this medicine.
hp.zh: 醫生提醒，有些孩子可能對這種藥過敏。

extra.en: My brother has an allergy to peanuts.
extra.zh: 我弟弟對花生過敏。

extra.en: People with an allergy to pollen often sneeze in spring.
extra.zh: 對花粉過敏的人春天常常打噴嚏。

near.fit: disease：疾病，不說 a disease to 某物。例：heart disease
an infection of／in 身體部位：感染，不用 to。例：an ear infection
a symptom of 某病：…的症狀，用 of。例：a symptom of the flu

fit: applause：掌聲，不可數（不加 a，也不加 s）；burst into applause、a round of applause

hp.en: The theater burst into applause when the play ended.
hp.zh: 演出結束時，劇場響起熱烈掌聲。

hp.en: The pianist received loud applause after her performance.
hp.zh: 鋼琴家演奏完後，獲得熱烈的掌聲。

extra.en: The audience gave the singer loud applause.
extra.zh: 觀眾給了歌手熱烈的掌聲。

extra.en: Let's give our teacher a big round of applause.
extra.zh: 讓我們給老師熱烈的掌聲。

near.fit: cheer：歡呼聲，可數，通常用 cheers 或 a cheer。例：loud cheers
clap：拍一下手的聲音，可數（a clap）。例：a clap of thunder
compliment：讚美，可數（pay 人 a compliment）。例：Thanks for the compliment.

hp.en: Kevin could feel his boss's hostility in every meeting.
hp.zh: 每次開會，凱文都感受得到老闆的敵意。

hp.en: The villagers showed hostility toward strangers who broke their rules.
hp.zh: 村民對違反規矩的外地人充滿敵意。

extra.en: The new student was surprised by the hostility of some classmates.
extra.zh: 新同學對部分同學的敵意感到驚訝。

extra.en: The two countries ended years of hostility with a peace deal.
extra.zh: 兩國以和平協議結束了多年的敵對。

hp.en: His friends said it was reckless to drive so fast in the rain.
hp.zh: 朋友們說在雨中開這麼快太魯莽了。

hp.en: The young climber could be reckless, especially in bad weather.
hp.zh: 那位年輕登山者有時很魯莽，尤其是天氣不好的時候。

extra.en: The police stopped him for reckless driving.
extra.zh: 警察因為他魯莽駕駛而把他攔下。

extra.en: It was reckless of him to swim alone at night.
extra.zh: 他晚上一個人去游泳，實在太魯莽了。

zh: 驚慌失措的；手忙腳亂的

hp.en: The boy was frantic when he couldn't find his passport.
hp.zh: 男孩找不到護照，急得要命。

hp.en: My aunt was frantic with worry when her son did not come home.
hp.zh: 兒子沒回家，阿姨擔心得快瘋了。

extra.en: The mother was frantic when she lost her child at the mall.
extra.zh: 那位媽媽在購物中心找不到孩子，急得不得了。

extra.en: We made a frantic call to the vet when our dog got sick.
extra.zh: 狗生病時，我們慌張地打電話給獸醫。

hp.en: The gang leader was a notorious criminal who escaped from prison.
hp.zh: 那名幫派老大是逃獄的惡名昭彰罪犯。

hp.en: This market is notorious for selling fake watches.
hp.zh: 這個市場以賣假錶而惡名昭彰。

extra.en: This road is notorious for traffic accidents.
extra.zh: 這條路以車禍頻傳出了名。

extra.en: The city is notorious for its heavy traffic.
extra.zh: 這座城市的交通壅塞是出了名的。

fit: be reliant on 人或物：依賴…（一定接 on）

hp.en: The young man was too reliant on his father's money.
hp.zh: 那個年輕人太依賴父親的錢。

hp.en: Kevin became less reliant on his classmates' notes after his first year.
hp.zh: 一年級之後，凱文比較不依賴同學的筆記了。

extra.en: Many people are too reliant on their phones.
extra.zh: 很多人太依賴手機了。

extra.en: Our town is reliant on tourism.
extra.zh: 我們鎮靠觀光業維生。

near.fit: reliable：可靠的，形容人或東西值得信賴，不接 on。例：a reliable friend
be confident in／of 某事：對…有信心，不接 on。例：confident of winning
be faithful to 人：對…忠實，用 to 不用 on。例：faithful to his wife

fit: linger + 地點或時間：逗留、揮之不去（不及物，不直接接受詞）

hp.en: My friends like to linger in the park after dinner.
hp.zh: 朋友們喜歡晚餐後在公園逗留。

hp.en: The smell of fried fish seemed to linger in the kitchen all day.
hp.zh: 煎魚的味道似乎整天都在廚房裡揮之不去。

extra.en: We like to linger at the café after school.
extra.zh: 放學後我們喜歡在咖啡廳逗留。

extra.en: Sad memories can linger for a long time.
extra.zh: 悲傷的回憶可能會縈繞很久。

near.fit: postpone 某事：把事情延後，後面要接受詞。例：postpone the meeting
inhabit 某地：居住於，及物，不說 inhabit in。例：Bears inhabit the forest.
occupy 空間或時間：佔據，及物，不說 occupy in。例：occupy two seats

fit: 某物 accumulate：東西慢慢累積、堆積（可以不接受詞）

hp.en: Dirty dishes began to accumulate in the kitchen sink.
hp.zh: 髒碗盤開始堆在廚房水槽裡。

hp.en: Leaves began to accumulate in the yard after the storm.
hp.zh: 暴風雨後，院子裡開始積起落葉。

extra.en: Snow began to accumulate on the roads.
extra.zh: 路上開始積雪。

extra.en: If you save a little every day, the money will accumulate.
extra.zh: 每天存一點，錢就會越積越多。

near.fit: reserve 某物：保留、預訂，後面要接受詞。例：reserve a table
obtain 某物：取得，後面要接受詞。例：obtain a license
acquire 某物：獲得、學到，後面要接受詞。例：acquire a new skill

fit: alienate 人 (from 某人)：使某人疏遠（及物，後面直接接人）

hp.en: His angry mood began to alienate his friends last year.
hp.zh: 去年，他的壞脾氣開始讓朋友疏遠他。

hp.en: Her choice to side with the company began to alienate her from her family.
hp.zh: 她選擇站在公司那邊，開始和家人疏遠。

extra.en: Rude comments can alienate your classmates.
extra.zh: 無禮的評論會讓同學疏遠你。

extra.en: The new rule may alienate some loyal customers.
extra.zh: 新規定可能會讓一些忠實顧客疏遠。

near.fit: drift apart／drift away：自己漸漸疏遠，不直接接人。例：Old friends drift apart.
depart (from) 某地：離開，不說 depart 人。例：depart from Taipei
retreat (from) 某處：撤退，不直接接人。例：retreat from the city

fit: amplify 聲音或事情：放大、增強（及物，後面要接受詞）

hp.en: The singer used a microphone to amplify her voice during the concert.
hp.zh: 演唱會上，歌手用麥克風放大自己的聲音。

hp.en: The band used large speakers to amplify the sound of the drums.
hp.zh: 樂團用大型喇叭放大鼓聲。

extra.en: The speaker can amplify the music for the whole room.
extra.zh: 喇叭能把音樂放大，讓整個房間都聽得到。

extra.en: Social media can amplify a small rumor.
extra.zh: 社群媒體可能把一個小謠言放大。

near.fit: 某物 rise：自己上升，不及物，不能接受詞。例：Prices rise.
問題 arise：問題出現，不及物，不能接受詞。例：Problems may arise.
某物 soar：快速上升，不及物，不能接受詞。例：Prices soared.

fit: adolescence：青春期（一段時期，不可數）；during／in adolescence

hp.en: My father spent his adolescence working on a farm.
hp.zh: 我爸爸的青春期都在農場工作。

hp.en: The famous writer showed her talent in early adolescence.
hp.zh: 那位知名作家在青春期早期就展現了才華。

extra.en: Many people grow quickly during adolescence.
extra.zh: 很多人在青春期長得很快。

extra.en: Writing a diary helped her get through adolescence.
extra.zh: 寫日記陪她度過了青春期。

near.fit: teenager：青少年（指人，可數），不說 during teenager。例：a teenager of 15
adolescent：青少年（指人，可數）。例：books for adolescents
youngster：小孩、年輕人（指人，可數）。例：a group of youngsters

fit: a disturbance：干擾、騷動（可數，可以加 a）

hp.en: A drunk man caused a disturbance in the restaurant.
hp.zh: 一名喝醉的男子在餐廳引起騷動。

hp.en: Scientists noticed a strange disturbance near the volcano.
hp.zh: 科學家察覺到火山附近有奇怪的擾動。

extra.en: The loud music next door was a disturbance to our sleep.
extra.zh: 隔壁的大聲音樂干擾了我們睡覺。

extra.en: The police were called to stop a disturbance in the park.
extra.zh: 警察被叫來平息公園裡的騷動。

near.fit: harm：傷害，不可數，不加 a（do harm to…）。例：do harm to your health
damage：東西被破壞的損害，不可數，不加 a。例：storm damage
chaos：一片混亂，不可數，不加 a（in chaos）。例：The room was in chaos.
